native_seed_if_empty_experiment.remaining: Native restart proves two canonical records remain engine-readable after normal close, not cross-process member-by-member equality or crash durability. It does not bind a Ferric profile-owner generation, exclude competing source or child writers, prove concurrent response/script/service-worker ordering, or certify durable seed publication.

It does not bind the copied cut to a Ferric profile-owner generation, exercise every network/script/service-worker/internal writer, exclude child writers, prove durable publication/crash recovery, or qualify production cookie capabilities.

native_t0_pre_and_post_cut_followup.scope: research-only synthetic source snapshot boundary fixture: one acknowledged source write occurs before the GetAllCookies request, then the pinned engine overlay inserts a second source write after the complete-list callback but before seeding; no user profile or real cookie values
native_t0_pre_and_post_cut_followup.remaining: This covers a controlled serial write before and after the copied-list boundary. experimental_unpublished_child_overlay.scope: research-only explicit default storage-partition/cookie-manager initialization without a child QWebEnginePage; no production writer lease or capability flag

native_unpublished_child_experiment.scope: two disk-loaded synthetic edge sources seed exactly into separate fresh persistent children before any child page exists; each child is then published to an about:blank page, rechecked natively, and reopened after normal close

The passing hook does not prove no browser-process writer, no competing application/native writer, an exclusive CookieMonster mutation lease, profile-owner generation, crash durability, exact cross-process member equality, or failure cleanup. native_cookie_owner_loss_experiment.scope: research-only cookie-copy callback ownership when the exact persistent source or destination QObject/profile is destroyed before the native reply is routed; legacy and older-expiry fixtures use only synthetic disposable data
native_cookie_owner_loss_experiment.remaining: A destination that may have been mutated when its owner is destroyed is disposable and is never reused. This proves only callback retirement for QObject/profile owner destruction on these synthetic paths. It does not simulate a bound-but-disconnected Mojo service, prove source generation or concurrent-writer exclusion, establish crash-durable seed publication, or enable a production cookie capability.

native_cookie_service_loss_experiment.scope: research-only loss of an in-flight CookieManager.GetAllCookies Mojo reply by disconnecting the bound cookie-manager receiver while the backing-store operation is pending; this simulates a disconnected pipe, not network-service process death, crash, or restart
native_cookie_service_loss_experiment.patch_application_check: The campaign used the source-pinned disposable Qt source tree, where the cumulative overlay was already applied. A reverse dry-run against that later cumulative tree failed on overlapping hunks; clean sequential application of this single patch from its intended intermediate overlay state was not independently re-run, so this entry does not claim standalone clean-tree reproducibility.

native_cookie_service_loss_experiment.remaining: This demonstrates conservative exactly-once timeout completion for the tested disconnected-pipe paths only. It does not simulate network-service process failure, service recreation, profile generation, concurrent writer exclusion, crash durability, atomic cleanup, exact unknown destination readback, general network failure, or complete WebRTC absence. Production cookie and WebRTC capabilities remain disabled.

experimental_rtc_admission_overlay.patch_application_check: Capability, seed-if-empty, RTC admission, fake-desktop and Qt Quick overlays were extracted from the pinned Qt 6.11.2 archive and applied in order with --fuzz=0 in a disposable temporary source tree.
experimental_rtc_admission_overlay.scope: candidate per-WebContents pending-to-active media request handoff, lease invalidation on request admission, fake-audio, fake-camera, combined fake audio/video and permission-denial routes with pending/active refusal, synthetic-frame delivery and stop cleanup, Linux pidfd-guarded renderer-loss lease invalidation, pending-count saturation and active-counter overflow/underflow poisoning, simulated fake-screen UI handoff, and real page-side screen:-3:0 capture with synthetic-frame delivery; not complete RTC absence or production support
experimental_rtc_admission_overlay.frame_assertion_note: The first offscreen presentation-callback assertion did not fire; the fixture now reads the actual track through MediaStreamTrackProcessor and requires nonzero frame dimensions, which passed in both configurations.
experimental_rtc_admission_overlay.renderer_loss_guard: Uses only QWebEnginePage::renderProcessPid() for the target; validates the exact isolated QtWebEngineProcess executable and a bounded ancestry of at most two intermediate QtWebEngineProcess helpers rooted at the fixture, captures every process start identity, opens a pidfd, repeats the ancestry/identity check, and only then signals the same pidfd. Chromium argv is not treated as stable evidence.
experimental_rtc_admission_overlay.remaining: The 2026-10-05 current fixture passed three fresh default and three strict-site-isolation runs on the pinned off-the-record Qt build. Results qualify only the exercised synthetic fake-device routes, bounded Qt counter handoffs, registry cases and exact renderer-loss cleanup. Physical camera/microphone devices, untested renderer/activity creation paths and capture categories, callback loss, full patch-chain reconstruction, production Rust ownership and shipping release qualification remain open. Synthetic capture uses Chromium's fixed fake devices only and never selects an OS capture source. These runs do not prove complete WebRTC absence; production remains disabled.

experimental_rtc_fake_desktop_overlay.scope: disposable fake-ID-only DesktopCaptureDevice subclass with bounded 640x480 synthetic frame generation for a native screen:-3:0 media-route experiment; never selects an OS capturer
experimental_rtc_fake_desktop_overlay.patch_application_check: The synthetic fake-source implementation was built into the isolated Qt engine used by the focused native and strict-site-isolation probes.
experimental_rtc_fake_desktop_overlay.runtime_result: Both focused configurations observed a nonzero synthetic video frame on the captured track, refused an empty lease while the track was live, and observed stop cleanup; no OS capture source was selected.

experimental_rtc_quick_bridge_overlay.patch_application_check: The current patch passed a zero-fuzz reverse dry run against the pinned Qt Quick source, rebuilt the isolated QtWebEngineQuick library, and loaded it through the research install prefix.
experimental_rtc_quick_bridge_overlay.scope: three fresh off-the-record Qt Quick exact-view owner runs for retained empty-registry leases, synthetic fake camera and combined capture routes, synthetic microphone admission in ApplicationWorld, lifecycle/foreign-thread guards, profile replacement, data-only peer registration and close semantics in ApplicationWorld, same-view document destruction, and renderer-loss invalidation; diagnostic capability research only

application_world_peer_probe.scope: Exact Qt Quick view creates and closes synthetic data-only RTCPeerConnections through ApplicationWorld; the pinned native peer registry observes them, and each dispatch revokes the held lease before script execution.

pinned_blink_exposure_audit.result: The pinned Blink IDL declares RTCPeerConnection and MediaDevices Exposed=Window; this excludes direct dedicated-worker API exposure on this revision, not all renderer/media activity.

application_world_capture_probe.scope: Exact Qt Quick view requests a synthetic fake-microphone stream from ApplicationWorld; the pending permission and active stream both block the diagnostic empty-registry lease, and track stop allows a fresh empty lease.

application_world_oopif_probe.scope: The exact Qt Quick view enumerates its WebEngineFrame child and dispatches RTCPeerConnection creation directly to that cross-origin frame in ApplicationWorld. Strict --site-per-process runs observe the child through the exact-view native registry with at least two frames and renderer processes, then reload and confirm a fresh empty registry. This validates one bounded child-frame path only.

chromium_capture_state_source_inspection.scope: This entry records static source inspection only. The separate test-only adapter bridge and its failed strict OOPIF run are recorded in child_frame_capture_adapter_followup below; neither qualifies a production absence certificate.

child_frame_capture_adapter_followup.scope: Test-only patched Qt/Chromium experiment. The strict OOPIF page and exact-view empty lease were reached, but invoking the synthetic child RenderFrameHost media counter did not make the complete-frame query report capture and did not emit the held-lease invalidation. An earlier native cross-origin getUserMedia attempt returned AbortError: Invalid state. This neither proves nor disproves real OOPIF capture; the private-API bridge is not qualified and is not used by Ferric production.

same_origin_child_control.result: A same-origin child frame under strict site isolation also returned AbortError: Invalid state; the document was complete, visible and secure, camera policy was allowed, both RFHs were active, and the permission callback was not observed.

controlled_cross_origin_capture_probe.scope: Disposable Qt 6.11.2 / Chromium strict-site-isolation probe with an off-the-record profile and Chromium's synthetic fake camera only. No physical camera, normal profile, or production code path was used.

grant_mode.result: Three fresh runs reached a live fake-camera track in the strict-site-isolated cross-origin child. The exact-view capture query saw activity and the inverse no-capture query refused; after track.stop(), the track ended, capture state cleared, and a fresh empty lease was admitted. The later direct-stderr trace confirmed the exact-origin MediaVideoCapture grant branch ran for https://top-a.localhost; the QML callback was bypassed in this deliberately forced-grant mode.

normal_mode_control.result: Historical pre-fix run. With grant/deny override flags absent, Qt resolved the child request as ASK and emitted the Quick permission signal. The QML handler received phase=42 and type=2, but the flattened WebEnginePermission.MediaVideoCapture expression evaluated undefined, so its comparison failed and the request returned AbortError: Invalid state. The later scoped-enum fix and passing normal-mode runs are recorded in permission_enum_fix.

deny_mode_negative_control.result: The direct trace confirmed the exact-origin DENIED branch executed for MediaVideoCapture. Chromium maps the denied/empty device result to the same browser-facing AbortError: Invalid state, so the error alone did not distinguish permission rejection from the earlier default path.

permission_enum_fix.cause: Qt 6.11.2's generated QML type metadata marks WebEnginePermission.PermissionType as a scoped enum. WebEnginePermission.MediaVideoCapture was undefined at runtime, so the QML handler received the child permission signal but its flattened enum comparisons never matched.
permission_enum_fix.implementation: Production FerricRequestPresentationController.qml now compares every supported request with WebEnginePermission.PermissionType.<name>. The disposable Qt Quick fixture uses the same scoped enum in its permission handler.
permission_enum_fix.result: Three fresh strict-site-isolation runs passed in normal permission mode. The child QML permission callback matched the scoped enum and granted the fake camera, then the exact-view capture query observed the live track; stop/clear cleanup and a fresh empty lease followed. The final fixture marker records childCaptureTrack=true childPermissionCallback=true.

child_frame_real_media_permission_follow.current_scope_update: The earlier scope/findings record normal-mode failures before the QML enum fix. Qt 6.11.2's WebEnginePermission.PermissionType is scoped, so flattened WebEnginePermission.MediaVideoCapture was undefined and did not match the child permission signal. Ferric's production presentation controller and the disposable fixture now use WebEnginePermission.PermissionType.<name>. Three strict-site-isolation runs with grant/deny override flags absent passed: the ordinary QML callback matched and granted the child video permission, a real fake-camera track became live, exact-view capture state was observed/refused as expected, and track-stop cleanup restored a fresh empty lease. This resolves the child permission handoff and demonstrates this scoped capture/observer route, but the observer still uses private Chromium state in a disposable Qt overlay and does not establish complete RTC absence, production Rust lifecycle ownership, or a Clear certificate. Keep production live retention disabled.

findings.root_cause: QML compared the scoped Qt 6.11.2 WebEnginePermission.PermissionType against an undefined flattened enum property.

child_frame_real_media_permission_follow.scope: The earlier strict-site-isolation, same-process and same-origin child failures are retained as historical evidence and were caused by a production QML permission-handler enum comparison bug, not an identified Chromium media-device rejection. Qt 6.11.2 generated QML metadata marks WebEnginePermission.PermissionType as scoped; the flattened member was undefined. After switching production and probe handlers to WebEnginePermission.PermissionType.<name>, three fresh strict-site-isolation runs with test-only grant/deny flags absent passed: the QML callback granted the child fake camera, exact-view capture query observed activity and refused empty admission, and track stop cleared capture before fresh empty admission. This resolves the tested child permission handoff. The activity observer still relies on private Chromium state in a disposable Qt overlay and does not prove exhaustive RTC/media absence, production Rust lifecycle ownership, callback-loss handling, or a Clear certificate. Keep production live retention disabled.

experimental_rtc_quick_bridge_overlay.remaining: In the pinned Chromium source, RTCPeerConnection.close() closes the transport but does not unregister the peer handler while its object remains in the live document; the fixture confirmed registration remained and same-view reload/context destruction allowed a fresh empty lease. The tested synthetic camera and combined routes, synthetic microphone admission from ApplicationWorld, and a frame-targeted cross-origin ApplicationWorld peer under strict site isolation passed the diagnostic Qt Quick bridge; three strict two-process runs observed the peer and clean child-context teardown. These do not qualify physical devices or complete RTC absence. The Qt Quick renderProcessTerminated bridge releases held/pending state with generation checks so a racing native invalidation is emitted once. Other renderer/media/capture categories, callback loss, production Rust ownership, and shipping/release qualification remain open; no production capability flag is enabled.

current_patch_qualification: v8 base retains its scoped mid-copy rejection evidence. Separate disposable seed-if-empty, post-snapshot-write and page-free-child overlays passed their pinned native fixtures and 40/53/33/59/59 regressions; they do not qualify source/child writer ownership, crash durability, merge or production RTC admission. On 2026-10-05 the current native RTC fixture passed three fresh default and three strict-site-isolation runs, including synthetic camera/combined media and bounded pidfd renderer-loss invalidation; the current Qt Quick exact-owner patch passed zero-fuzz applicability, isolated build/install and three fresh runs including synthetic camera, microphone and combined permission routes. On 2026-10-06 the same Qt Quick bridge/fixture passed three additional fresh runs with its data-only peer created and closed through ApplicationWorld. On 2026-10-07 it passed another three runs with synthetic microphone pending/active/stop handling through ApplicationWorld, followed by three strict-site-isolation cross-origin child-frame peer runs using QML WebEngineFrame.runJavaScript in ApplicationWorld; the exact owner observed at least two frames/processes and same-view reload cleared the peer. A separate default-configuration run also passed. These scoped results add feasibility evidence only, not a complete RTC-absence certificate or production capability. Production disabled.
